no_ladder.description: Why no judged question is written, or null: the topic has no main figure or event (none, or several with none the main one); nothing in it can be checked on a date (for an event: no date given and no period named, unless it is a pending regulatory decision, which is due at the company's current fiscal year-end); a company's figure for a quarter or a half-year; a figure for a period that is not one fiscal or calendar year, such as a survey's rolling twelve months, with no publication day in the topic or the item; a figure for a year that has already ended on the item's day; a figure for a year beyond next year (unless the topic's opens_as is binding_obligation); or the question belongs to another company or to a matter no listed theme covers (name it). Exactly one of no_ladder and ladder is null (checked by code).

question.description: The one judged question: one figure for a named period, or one event. For a figure it names the period covered or the day measured at, and the material that settles it.

object.description: The company's ticker, or a theme id from the themes listed in the request. Nothing else: a question with another object is returned as no_ladder.

not_judged.description: Every other part of the topic's description and outcome that the question leaves out (a second figure or event, a condition, a comparison); empty only when the question leaves nothing of either out.

event.description: For an event; else null. Exactly one of event and figure is not null (checked by code).

happened.description: The condition under which the event the question asks about has happened by the due day.

ruled_out.description: Who can rule the event as a whole out before the due day, and how. Null only when no one's decision can. No condition is written for what is left.

by_whom.description: The company, authority, court or party whose decision it would be.

decision.description: One full sentence that names them and says what they decide against the event as a whole, or that they formally abandon or withdraw it, after the item's day. Never the due day arriving without the event.

figure.description: For one figure: its unit, the year it covers, exactly five ranges and, for a company, the favourable end; else null.

unit.description: other when the unit is none of the listed; the question then names it.

year.description: The one year the figure covers: FY2027 for a company's figure (its fiscal year); 2026 for a theme's figure (a calendar year). Code refuses the other form.

lo.description: Inclusive lower bound, a number; null for the lowest range only.

hi.description: Exclusive upper bound, a number; null for the highest range only.

favourable_end.description: For a company's figure: higher or lower, the end that is good for its business (n/a is refused). For a theme's figure: n/a (higher or lower is refused).

favourable_why.description: For a company's figure: one sentence on why that end is good for the business; it may not be empty. For a theme's figure: empty.

words.description: The item's own words for what the figure or event is measured against.

kind.description: expected: what the market expects. last_reported: for a figure only, the amount most recently reported for the same quantity, when the item states no expectation.

value.description: The number the item states, in the figure's unit; the lower end of a stated range. Null when the item gives it in words alone.

value_to.description: The upper end of a stated range; else null.

due_day_basis.description: For a figure: stated or expected_publication. For an event: stated, or period_end (the last day of the period the topic names, or the company's current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision with no date).
